project.name: FriBidi
project.commit_note: The staged source reviewed here is the prepared clean checkout at `3ccfb68d2ce9ace5e83fb96b6da45de637522804`, not an exact checkout of the sample metadata's `vulnerable_commit` (`441c173cbb3562f4b89745ac2bbaaa632b4fe9f5`). This prepared tree still contains the reviewed vulnerable merge predicates in `lib/fribidi-bidi.c:108-113` and `127-135`, and the saved AddressSanitizer line map (`merge_with_prev:93`, `compact_list:113`, `fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex:1261`) matches it. The staged `patch.diff` adds the missing `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(...)` predicate to those same `compact_neutrals()` and `compact_list()` merge sites; the known `441c173...` vs prepared-tree difference around the `PDI` branch at `lib/fribidi-bidi.c:707-710` is outside this witness, which contains no `PDI` run.

classification.classification_note: The reproduced manifestation is an 8-byte heap-use-after-free WRITE into a freed `FriBidiRun`'s `next_isolate` field. The missing obligation is the same in both compaction helpers: they merge adjacent runs by resolved type/level without requiring equal `isolate_level`.

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5372192033472512 Project: fribidi Fuzz Target: fribidi-fuzzer Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free WRITE 8 Crash State: merge_with_prev compact_list fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.normalized: The staged 268-byte witness is interpreted as 67 little-endian `FriBidiChar` words: `U+202D`, `33×U+202A`, `U+202D`, `27×U+202A`, `0x20202020`, `U+2068`, `U+2020`, `U+000A`, `0xFFFFFF20`. FriBidi's generated bidi-type table maps both out-of-range words to default `LTR`, so `run_list_encode_bidi_types()` materializes runs `[LRO][LRE×33][LRO][LRE×27][LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]`. The 62 explicit LRO/LRE controls raise the current embedding level to 124 before the FSI suffix. `fribidi_get_par_embedding_levels_ex()` then assigns `RL_LEVEL=124` to the pre-FSI `LTR` run and to the `FSI` run itself; the FSI opens isolate level 1 for the following `ON` run but, because it has no matching `PDI`, its computed `new_level` overflows past 125 and the active embedding level stays 124. Building isolate links therefore yields outer chain `LTR -> FSI -> tail LTR` and inner chain `ON -> BS`. Vulnerable `compact_neutrals()` next merges the adjacent `FSI` and `ON` runs even though their isolate levels differ, because it checks only `RL_LEVEL` and neutralness. `merge_with_prev()` rewires `FSI.next_isolate` to `BS`, clears `BS.prev_isolate`, and frees the `ON` run, breaking the reciprocity of the isolate side links while the tail outer `LTR` still points back to `FSI`. Neutral resolution later rewrites the merged `FSI` run and the `BS` run to resolved type `LTR` but does not rebuild isolate links. During the final `compact_list()` pass, FriBidi first merges the two outer `LTR` runs and frees the merged `FSI` run while the tail outer `LTR` still keeps it in `prev_isolate`; the next `compact_list()` merge then treats `BS` and that tail `LTR` as mergeable same-type same-level neighbors and `merge_with_prev()` writes `second->prev_isolate->next_isolate` through the freed run. AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-use-after-free WRITE at `lib/fribidi-bidi.c:93`. The fix adds the missing `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list->prev) == RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(list)` guard to both `compact_neutrals()` and `compact_list()`.

source.description: First project-side statement that consumes the attacker-controlled 32-bit words and materializes the bidi-type stream later fed into run encoding and compaction.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 268-byte witness (sha256 `1e7fc67ab461242b8413c731098783021c709750a27b3acf3f86885e91e7a2de`). The harness casts it to 67 little-endian `FriBidiChar` words. This statement reads them sequentially and materializes the vulnerability-relevant sequence `U+202D`, `33×U+202A`, `U+202D`, `27×U+202A`, `0x20202020`, `U+2068`, `U+2020`, `U+000A`, `0xFFFFFF20`; the generated bidi-type lookup uses `LTR` as its default table value, so both out-of-range words become `LTR` on the witnessed path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-derived bidi-type transitions are materialized here as heap-allocated `FriBidiRun` objects linked into `main_run_list`. The run later freed and overwritten on the crashing path originates from this allocation path; AddressSanitizer's allocation stack points to `new_run()` called from this function.

root_cause.code:
if (RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list)
    &&
    ((RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list)
      || (FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list->prev))
          && FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list)))))
    && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET
    && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET)
  list = merge_with_prev (list);
root_cause.description: First witness-specific invariant violation. `compact_neutrals()` merges adjacent neutral runs solely on resolved level/type and bracket state, without requiring equal `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL`. On this witness it merges `FSI` (outer isolate chain) with the following `ON` run (inner isolate chain), corrupting the isolate-side links that later turn a subsequent compaction merge into a use-after-free write.
root_cause.note: The staged patch adds `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL (list)` to this exact predicate and to the analogous `compact_list()` predicate. The first bad merge on the witnessed path happens here; the later crashing merge repeats the same missing obligation in `compact_list()`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The later `compact_list()` merge reaches a run whose `prev_isolate` still aliases a `FriBidiRun` freed by the immediately preceding merge, so this write stores through a dangling pointer.
sink.note: ASan reports `WRITE of size 8` at this statement. The reported address is 48 bytes inside a 56-byte `FriBidiRun` region, which matches the `next_isolate` field offset in `struct _FriBidiRunStruct` (`prev_isolate` at offset 40, `next_isolate` at offset 48 on this 64-bit build).

parser_admitted.description: The attacker-derived bidi and bracket arrays have been accepted by FriBidi and are being encoded into the run list that the vulnerable compaction helpers mutate.

fine_trace.note: The project first consumes the 67 `FriBidiChar` words here and maps them to bidi classes. The vulnerability-relevant sequence becomes `[LRO][LRE×33][LRO][LRE×27][LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]`: `U+202D` is `LRO`, `U+202A` is `LRE`, `U+2068` is `FSI`, `U+2020` is `ON`, `U+000A` is `BS`, and both out-of-range words (`0x20202020`, `0xFFFFFF20`) take the generated table's default `LTR` class.

The same witness words are also materialized into bracket metadata. The suffix runs that later enter the bad merges all end up with `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`, so the bracket clauses in `compact_neutrals()` and `compact_list()` do not block compaction on the crashing path.

FriBidi turns the attacker-controlled type/bracket arrays into heap-allocated `FriBidiRun` nodes and groups only consecutive equal non-isolate types. For this witness the main logical run order is `[LRO][LRE×33][LRO][LRE×27][LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]`. These `FriBidiRun` allocations are the heap objects later freed and reused by `merge_with_prev()`.

The 62 explicit controls in the prefix (`2×LRO` and `60×LRE`) are processed here. Starting from base level 0, each one raises the current embedding level by 2, so after the last explicit run the current `level` is 124. The explicit runs themselves are then removed from `main_run_list`, leaving the surviving non-explicit suffix runs `[LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]` to carry that high current level forward.

The FSI suffix is assigned here. The FSI run itself gets `RL_LEVEL = 124` and `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL = 0`. Its lookahead never finds a matching `PDI`, so the trailing out-of-range `LTR` word stays nested under the FSI's own `isolate_count` and `fsi_base_level` remains 0; with current `level = 124`, that yields `new_level = 126`, which is rejected as overflow. FriBidi still increments the running `isolate_level` to 1, so the following `ON` run inherits `RL_LEVEL = 124` but `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL = 1`.

FriBidi next builds side links only within equal `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL`. On the witness path this yields outer chain `LTR(before FSI) -> FSI -> LTR(after newline)` for isolate level 0, and inner chain `ON -> BS` for isolate level 1. The main `prev/next` list is still `[LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]`, but `prev_isolate`/`next_isolate` now encode a different partition.

fine_trace.code:
if (RL_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_LEVEL (list)
    &&
    ((RL_TYPE (list->prev) == RL_TYPE (list)
      || (FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list->prev))
          && FRIBIDI_IS_NEUTRAL (RL_TYPE (list)))))
    && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET
    && RL_BRACKET_TYPE(list->prev) == FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET)
  list = merge_with_prev (list);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. In the first `compact_neutrals(main_run_list)` pass, the adjacent `FSI` run (outer isolate chain) and `ON` run (inner isolate chain) satisfy the visible predicate: both are neutral, both are at `RL_LEVEL = 124`, and both have `FRIBIDI_NO_BRACKET`. Because the helper does not also require `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL (list->prev) == RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL (list)`, it merges them across the isolate boundary.

The bad cross-isolate merge from step 7 rewires the side links as if `FSI` and `ON` belonged to the same isolate chain. `ON.next_isolate` is `BS`, so the merge clears `BS.prev_isolate` to `NULL`, sets `FSI.next_isolate = BS`, and frees the `ON` run. The outer tail `LTR` run is not touched and still keeps `prev_isolate = FSI`, so the isolate-link reciprocity is now broken.

Later neutral resolution turns both the merged `FSI` run and the `BS` run into resolved type `LTR` because their surrounding directions both resolve to `LTR`. FriBidi does not rebuild `prev_isolate`/`next_isolate` after this rewrite, so the main-list order becomes `LTR(level124,iso0) -> LTR(level124,iso0) -> LTR(level0,iso1) -> LTR(level0,iso0)` while the side links remain corrupted (`mergedFSI.next_isolate = BS`, `BS.prev_isolate = NULL`, tail `LTR.prev_isolate = mergedFSI`).

In the final `compact_list(main_run_list)` pass, FriBidi first merges the two `LTR`/level-124 outer runs: the original outer `LTR` and the merged `FSI` run. Because the earlier corruption left `second->next_isolate = BS` instead of the tail outer `LTR`, this merge repairs `BS.prev_isolate` but never updates the tail outer `LTR`. `fribidi_free(second)` therefore frees the merged `FSI` run while the tail outer `LTR` still keeps it in `prev_isolate`, creating the dangling lifetime state consumed at the sink.

The same missing isolate-level guard recurs in `compact_list()`. After step 10, the adjacent `BS` run (now `LTR`, `level 0`, `isolate_level 1`) and the tail outer `LTR` run (`level 0`, `isolate_level 0`) satisfy this predicate, so `compact_list()` performs a second cross-isolate merge even though the tail run's `prev_isolate` is already dangling.

Sink. In the second final merge from step 11, `second` is the tail outer `LTR` run and its `prev_isolate` still points to the merged `FSI` run freed in step 10. Writing `next_isolate` through that stale `prev_isolate` pointer triggers the observed 8-byte heap-use-after-free WRITE at `merge_with_prev:93`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the missing `RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL(...)` equality to both `compact_neutrals()` and `compact_list()`, which blocks the step-7 and step-11 cross-isolate merges required by this witness.

evidence_limitations: Runtime disambiguation was disabled (`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`), so the specific run-state sequence is reconstructed statically from the staged PoC words, source, patch, and saved ASan/free/allocation traces rather than from marker instrumentation.

format.contract: Use the exact staged 268-byte witness file `poc` (sha256 `1e7fc67ab461242b8413c731098783021c709750a27b3acf3f86885e91e7a2de`). The harness casts it to 67 little-endian 32-bit `FriBidiChar` words: `U+202D`, `33×U+202A`, `U+202D`, `27×U+202A`, `0x20202020`, `U+2068`, `U+2020`, `U+000A`, `0xFFFFFF20`. FriBidi's generated bidi-type table maps both out-of-range words to default `LTR`, so the project-side type stream is `[LRO][LRE×33][LRO][LRE×27][LTR][FSI][ON][BS][LTR]`. That exact layout raises the explicit embedding level to 124 before the FSI, builds outer/inner isolate chains `LTR -> FSI -> tail LTR` and `ON -> BS`, triggers the bad cross-isolate `compact_neutrals()` merge, and then reaches the later freeing and crashing `compact_list()` merges described above. The staged evidence does not justify a broader trigger class than this exact witness layout.
